row.team_price_text: Per transaction: $0.13 processing fee + payment method fee; no setup or monthly fees
row.evidence: Adyen's Customer Area supports SAML 2.0 SSO, but SSO users must be created in the Customer Area or with a Management API request; no SCIM endpoint is documented in the docs index or API reference.
row.notes: New row. Adyen has no seat-based plans: it charges per transaction ($0.13 processing fee plus a payment-method fee, no setup or monthly fees), so team and per-user price fields stay null. SAML SSO for the Customer Area needs a company account (not a merchant account); existing users are not switched to SSO automatically and there is no documented JIT creation. Users can be listed, created and updated (including active=false to deactivate) through the Management API v3 at company or merchant level with an API key holding the 'Management API—Users read and write' role; no IdP connector uses it. Okta's OIN 'Adyen' app is SWA only. 'None' is by absence (rule 5).

scim.notes: No SCIM endpoint appears in the docs index (docs.adyen.com/llms.txt), the SSO guides or the Management API reference; users for SSO are created manually or via the Management API. 'false' is by absence (rule 5).

user_api.notes: Live base URL is not quoted here; only the test endpoint destination URL was captured.

endpoints.purpose: Create a company-level user (loginMethod Email or SSO)
Update user details, roles, account access, active flag

limitations.text: No DELETE user endpoint is listed; users are deactivated (active=false or Deactivate user in the Customer Area) rather than deleted.

okta.notes: OIN 'Adyen' app marks only SWA as supported (read from page markup); SAML, SCIM and provisioning items are unchecked.

entra.notes: No Entra gallery tutorial found (learn.microsoft.com adyen-tutorial URLs return 404). Adyen's SSO guide covers Azure as a custom SAML app.

google.notes: Adyen's SSO guide lists Google as a SAML IdP; no Google catalogue entry was checked.

fallbacks.notes: jit=false because the SSO guide requires creating SSO users (Customer Area or Management API) before they can log in, and existing users must be migrated.
